options.name: Stage rail plus persistent tool tabs
options.desktopBehavior: Clicking a different stage selects its first available tool. The active drawer then presents a permanent horizontal sibling-tool row.

keyboard.tab: Native Tab moves through stage buttons and, while open, sibling tool buttons.
keyboard.arrows: No custom arrow-key movement is implemented for rail or tool navigation.
keyboard.enterSpace: Activates a stage or sibling tool.
keyboard.escape: Application Escape handling closes the drawer or open layer menu.
keyboard.focusReturn: ToolDrawer focuses its heading when opened; close logic targets the active sibling button, which is unmounted with the drawer.

options.pointerHover: Stage hover presents a tooltip; it does not expose sibling tools.
options.touch: The tool row is horizontally scrollable, but its scrollbar is hidden.
options.mapContract: Map and drawer remain in one workspace; no routing.
advantages: Sibling names visible without opening another control
Per-tool availability and attention are visible
costs: Active tool appears in the rail stage state, drawer title, and selected tool row
Four-tool row is wider than the drawer and its scrollbar is hidden

options.name: Rail flyout
options.desktopBehavior: Keep the 88 px four-stage rail. Clicking a different stage preserves current behavior by selecting the stage's first available tool and opening its tool flyout. Clicking the active stage opens/closes its list without changing the current tool. The flyout contains the stage name and vertically listed tools. Selecting a sibling changes the drawer in place and closes the flyout.
options.activeToolDisplay: Drawer header remains the single persistent tool title/description. The selected tool is marked in the flyout while open.
options.availability: Keep unavailable tools visible with the existing reason and attention/result badge. Do not let opening a flyout load the tool.

keyboard.tab: Tab reaches each named stage button; normal Tab/Shift+Tab reaches named tool choices when open.
keyboard.arrows: Within the flyout, Up/Down move among tool choices; Home/End move to first/last. Disabled tools remain discoverable and announce why but cannot activate.
keyboard.enterSpace: Enter/Space on a stage opens/closes its flyout. Enter/Space on a tool selects it.
keyboard.focusReturn: Escape returns focus to the stage trigger. Tool selection transfers focus to the current tool heading. Closing the drawer returns focus to the active stage button.
keyboard.roles: Use a stage button with accurate aria-haspopup/aria-expanded and a named navigation/menu surface with selected/current item semantics. Implement the expected arrow-key model if using menu roles.

options.pointerHover: Hover may provide an optional preview but is not required to open or operate the list; click always works.
options.touch: Tap stage to open, tap named tool to select. No hover-dependent action.

responsiveBehavior.atOrAbove1280: Flyout anchored to the clicked rail stage, over the drawer edge; map and drawer dimensions do not change.
responsiveBehavior.1024To1279: Same model with the same overlay behavior; retain tool labels and status text.
responsiveBehavior.640To1023: Touch-sized click popover; rail stays vertical; no hover dependency.
responsiveBehavior.below640: Bottom rail remains. A stage tap uses the existing drawer sheet footprint as a tool chooser; selecting a tool returns to the single-tool sheet.

options.directNavigation: Direct actions continue to set activeTool/drawer state in App and bypass the flyout.
options.lazyLoading: Tool labels/icons and menu open do not import chunks. Existing dynamic import starts only after the existing tool selection/render boundary is reached.

interactionCost.coldSwitch: A tool switch from a closed active-stage flyout takes two activations: open stage list, choose sibling.
interactionCost.differentStageDefault: One stage activation selects the existing first-available default and exposes siblings.
interactionCost.openFlyout: Selecting an item from an already-open flyout takes one activation.
interactionCost.mapAndDrawerContext: No route or map resize; drawer title/content changes only when tool selection changes.

commonTransitions.note: Simulate stage keeps current first-available default behavior.
Open active Simulate flyout, choose Experiments.
Analyze stage selects first available; requires Interference to be eligible. Otherwise the default remains RF Diagnostics.
Open Analyze flyout, choose RF Diagnostics.
Open Review flyout, choose Run history.
Open Analyze flyout, choose Building entry.

tradeoffs: Removes a persistent row and fits four tool names vertically.
Same-stage closed-menu switches add one activation versus current tabs.
Stage defaults and direct navigation remain familiar.
No telemetry proves a need for recents or hotkeys; defer both.

options.name: Expandable rail
options.desktopBehavior: Expand the selected stage to show its tool buttons under its stage label. Choose a tool from the expanded group.

keyboard.tab: Tab moves through stages; expanded stage reveals tool buttons in the normal order.
keyboard.arrows: Up/Down can move within a stage list if a roving focus model is deliberately implemented; otherwise native Tab remains.
keyboard.enterSpace: Toggle stage expansion or activate a tool.
keyboard.focusReturn: Return to the stage button when collapsed.

options.mapImpact: A persistent expanded rail needs roughly 208–248 px total width instead of 88 px, reducing map width by roughly 120–160 px. An overlay variant is effectively a persistent flyout.
options.directNavigation: Direct actions update active stage and expanded tool list without extra selection.
options.lazyLoading: Expansion exposes metadata only; select tool to trigger its existing lazy boundary.
options.interactionCost: One activation for siblings once expanded; two to expand a different stage and select a non-default tool.
costs: Consumes horizontal map area when expanded
Longer stage rail and more visible navigation chrome

options.name: Compact stage selector plus current-tool dropdown
options.desktopBehavior: Keep the current stage rail and replace the persistent row with a current-tool dropdown in the drawer header.

keyboard.tab: Tab to stage buttons and the labeled current-tool selector.
keyboard.arrows: Native select behavior or expected popover menu arrows.
keyboard.escape: Close dropdown and restore focus to its trigger.
keyboard.focusReturn: Return to the tool selector or heading after selection.

options.touch: Tap dropdown, then choose a sibling; below 640 px use a sheet/picker.
options.mapImpact: No rail width increase and no map resize; header receives a permanent compact selector.
options.directNavigation: Direct destinations update the stage rail and current-tool control.
options.lazyLoading: Opening selector does not load tools; choose to activate the current boundary.
options.interactionCost: Same-stage cold switch takes two activations; switching stages to a non-default tool can take stage selection plus dropdown open plus tool selection.
advantages: Smaller vertical cost than a full row
Tool name remains adjacent to the drawer title
costs: Rail does not own tool selection
Another persistent selector shares the crowded top area

options.name: Two-column temporary stage/tool chooser
options.desktopBehavior: A rail activation opens a temporary stage column and sibling-tool column.

keyboard.tab: Tab enters the chooser and traverses both columns.
keyboard.arrows: Left/Right change columns; Up/Down move within the active column.

options.touch: Tap stage and then tool in a larger bottom sheet.
options.mapImpact: A 280–320 px temporary overlay covers more of the map/drawer edge than a single flyout.
options.lazyLoading: Metadata-only chooser; tool select triggers existing chunk.
options.interactionCost: Two activations from a closed chooser; one after a stage column is already active.
advantages: Makes the hierarchy explicit across all stages
costs: Larger overlay, more navigation surface, and more map occlusion

options.name: Persistent nested rail with every stage's tools visible
options.desktopBehavior: Show each stage and its complete tool list permanently in a nested left navigation column.

keyboard.tab: Tab traverses all stages and all 13 tools on every workspace screen.
keyboard.arrows: A treeview needs a full tree keyboard model; plain links/buttons use native Tab order.
keyboard.escape: No persistent menu to close; dismiss overlays only.
keyboard.focusReturn: Direct tool activation focuses the active tool heading.

options.touch: Nested lists remain available, but a dedicated mobile sheet would still be needed.
options.mapImpact: Four stages plus 13 tool links need substantially more than 88 px, or force dense icon-only navigation.
options.directNavigation: Direct actions select the corresponding tool and its stage.
options.lazyLoading: Items expose metadata only; activating one uses its existing lazy boundary.
options.interactionCost: One activation to select any visible tool.
advantages: All sibling tools are continuously discoverable
costs: Persistent navigation dominates the map-first layout
Consumes the most horizontal map width
Dense and difficult to scan on tablet and mobile

options.name: Stage rail plus workspace-wide tool palette
options.desktopBehavior: Keep stage-only rail and add a searchable command palette that lists tools across all stages.

keyboard.tab: Tab reaches the palette trigger; focus is managed inside the searchable dialog while open.
keyboard.arrows: Up/Down move through filtered results; typing narrows the list.
keyboard.enterSpace: Enter selects a result; Space follows the input/button native behavior.
keyboard.escape: Escape closes the palette and restores focus to its trigger.
keyboard.focusReturn: Return focus to the trigger after dismissal; focus the tool heading after selection.

options.touch: Use a searchable full-width sheet on phone.
options.mapImpact: No persistent map resize, but opening the palette covers workspace content.
options.directNavigation: Direct actions continue to bypass the palette.
options.lazyLoading: Search indexes metadata only; selection follows the current lazy boundary.
options.interactionCost: At least two activations plus search/scan for most users; frequent experts may benefit from a shortcut.
advantages: Can find a known tool without first knowing its stage
costs: Adds a new global control and modal/search interaction
Weakens stage-to-tool learning for first-time users
No telemetry supports prioritizing search over visible sibling choices

railCapacityAlternatives.name: Stage-only rail (current baseline)
railCapacityAlternatives.assessment: Keeps the 88 px rail compact, but cannot own tool selection. The permanent drawer row currently supplies sibling navigation.

railCapacityAlternatives.name: Click-to-expand stage flyout (selected capacity pattern)
railCapacityAlternatives.assessment: A click/tap opens up to four named tools and transfers the drawer row's discovery and availability/attention jobs without persistent map cost.

railCapacityAlternatives.name: Hover/focus-open stage flyout
railCapacityAlternatives.assessment: Fast for pointer users but can open accidentally, is hard to stabilize across the rail-to-flyout gap, and does not translate cleanly to touch. Focus may reveal a preview; click/tap remains dependable.

railCapacityAlternatives.name: Two-column temporary stage/tool chooser
railCapacityAlternatives.assessment: Makes both levels explicit but covers more of the map and adds a second navigation column.

railCapacityAlternatives.name: Persistent nested rail
railCapacityAlternatives.assessment: Keeps every sibling visible and enables one-activation selection, but 13 tool labels dominate the left edge and reduce map width at every viewport.

railCapacityAlternatives.name: Workspace-wide searchable tool palette
railCapacityAlternatives.assessment: Helps experts who know a tool name, but adds a global launcher and search mode without evidence that it solves first-time stage/tool discovery.

decision.why: It replaces the permanent tool row while retaining map width, stage semantics, sibling discovery, availability/attention, current-tool title, direct navigation, and lazy boundaries.
decision.qualification: The closed-menu same-stage cost rises from one to two activations. A stage click to its existing first-available default remains one activation. Confirm the tradeoff with expert users during 8B review.

frequentTransitions.evidence: No product telemetry or user observation dataset was available; these are workflow hypotheses.
frequentTransitions.recommendation: Do not invent Recent tools or keyboard shortcuts in 8B. Evaluate switching feedback after the flyout is usable.

mapFirstContract: Tool selection updates the same drawer
decision.lastToolMemory: Current rail stage clicks select the first available tool; preserve that expectation for 8B. Do not add per-stage persisted last-tool state.
